title: Carboplatin AUC 4 and fluorouracil with radiotherapy
indication_text: Locally advanced head and neck squamous cell cancer when cisplatin-based treatment is unsuitable.
purpose: Chemotherapy is given with radiation to improve control of cancer in the head and neck. Your team confirms the treatment aim and why carboplatin is suitable for your circumstances.
schedule_label: Day 1: carboplatin; Days 1–4: 5-FU. Every 21 days ×3, during RT.
schedule_summary: Carboplatin AUC 4 on Day 1, with fluorouracil 600 mg/m²/day on Days 1–4, every 21 days for 3 cycles, only concurrently with radiotherapy.
administration_text: Carboplatin is given over 30 minutes on Day 1; its dose is calculated from kidney function. Fluorouracil runs continuously over 96 hours; the source also permits separate 22-hour infusions on Days 1–4. Confirm the actual pump or bag-change and disconnection times.
monitoring_summary: Before each cycle: full blood count, kidney and liver tests. Review weight, intake, swallowing, mouth symptoms, hands and feet. Measured kidney function is preferred when feasible; audiology is arranged when indicated.

agents.name: Carboplatin
agents.explanation: Carboplatin interferes with DNA repair and cell division. Its dose is calculated from kidney function. Blood counts can fall, including platelets that help stop bleeding. It is a different prescription from cisplatin. AUC is a prescribing target for drug exposure, not the number of milligrams in your bag; your clinical team calculates the dose using kidney function.
agents.watch: Report fever, unusual bruising or bleeding, marked tiredness or an infusion reaction.
risks: Low blood counts and serious infection

agents.name: Fluorouracil
agents.mechanism: Disrupts production of DNA and RNA
agents.explanation: Fluorouracil, often shortened to 5-FU, interferes with the building blocks used to make DNA and RNA, which cells need to grow. It runs through a vein over the prescribed hours. Dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPD) is an enzyme that breaks it down. Testing for DPD deficiency before treatment reduces risk but cannot rule out every severe reaction.
agents.watch: Report severe diarrhoea, mouth sores, chest pain, sudden confusion, sore palms or soles, or unexpectedly early severe symptoms.
risks: Low blood counts and serious infection
Rare severe neurological or early excessive toxicity

anatomy: Tiredness can affect activity and concentration. Balance activity and rest; report sudden confusion.

support.title: Preventing and treating sickness
support.text: Use the prescribed medicines for the active treatment day. The regimen is classified as high sickness risk.

support.title: Fluorouracil and your infusion
support.text: DPD testing checks for an enzyme deficiency that can increase toxicity. Normal testing does not eliminate risk. Call urgently for chest symptoms or unusually early severe diarrhoea, mouth soreness or confusion.

support.title: Mouth care and nutrition
support.text: Follow your unit’s oral-care plan. Tell the team early about mouth pain, weight loss, choking or difficulty eating and drinking. Dietetic and swallowing support can help.

support.title: Fever and sudden illness
support.text: Fever, shivering, sudden illness, unusual bleeding, new breathlessness, persistent vomiting or inability to drink needs urgent oncology advice. Severe chest pain, severe breathing difficulty, collapse or a seizure is an emergency: call 112/999.

support.title: Medicine review
support.text: Bring prescription, non-prescription and herbal medicines. Check interactions, allergies and any changes with the oncology pharmacist.

support.title: Recovery and practical support
support.text: Ask about fatigue, work, transport, caring responsibilities, emotional support and help with appointments.

evidence.title: Understanding the evidence
evidence.intro: The national regimen brings together research and specialist guidance for a specific treatment setting.
evidence.population: Locally advanced head and neck squamous cell cancer when cisplatin-based treatment is unsuitable.
evidence.comparison: Discuss the alternatives appropriate to your cancer and health.
evidence.interpretation: The GORTEC 94-01 evidence cited by NCCP concerns four-day carboplatin 70 mg/m² plus fluorouracil with radiation in advanced oropharyngeal cancer. Its numerical outcomes should not be treated as an exact estimate for every head and neck site or for the separate carboplatin AUC 4 schedule.
limitations: Different doses, disease settings and treatment sequences are not interchangeable.
Group study results cannot predict an individual outcome.

consent_support: Discuss treatment aim and alternatives, expected benefit and uncertainty, all listed drug risks, infection and emergency advice, blood and organ checks, support medicines, fertility and contraception, and the option of declining treatment. Discuss radiation-specific acute and late risks separately with radiation oncology, and DPD testing, infusion/line care and the pump schedule.
